metadata.focus: Original alternate-story corroboration and stale-count repair
metadata.notes: Eight replacement alternate leads, one pre-existing Oct6 alternate with missing evidence repaired. Distinguish event milestones from image dates, UTC/local times and multiday amounts. No full fact check or publication rights.

alternate_reviews.title: An immense snow-and-ice storm expands across the southern United States
alternate_reviews.location: Southern Plains and lower Mississippi Valley, United States
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On January 24, 2026, a major winter storm spread snow and freezing rain through the Southern Plains and Mid-South, disrupting travel and utilities while expanding eastward.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: WPC's meteorological review and contemporaneous AP impact reporting separately document the event; both ultimately reference shared NWS operational guidance.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Storm began January 23 in some areas and lasted through January 26; Pennsylvania's major snow mainly began Jan 25. Do not describe full multiday snowfall or ice totals as January 24 values.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original precipitation-type and surface-pressure analysis for January 24, with a freezing-rain corridor and valid times.

alternate_reviews.title: Mount Washington reports an extraordinary −109°F wind chill
alternate_reviews.location: Mount Washington summit, New Hampshire, United States
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: At 11:35 p.m. EST on February 3, 2023, Mount Washington Observatory's summit conditions page reported approximately −109°F wind chill amid exceptionally cold and windy conditions.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: Observatory supplied direct station air temperature/wind and computed wind chill; local reporting describes it but does not independently measure the summit.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Wind chill is calculated apparent temperature, not measured air temperature. Actual low of roughly −47°F occurred around 3 a.m. February 4. Reports use −108 or −109 for separate timestamps; all-time U.S. wind-chill record scope is unsettled.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original February 3–4 hourly temperature, winds and computed wind-chill chart with midnight marked.

alternate_reviews.title: A powerful Sierra Nevada blizzard begins on Leap Day
alternate_reviews.location: Sierra Nevada and Lake Tahoe, California and Nevada, United States
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On February 29, 2024, a powerful Pacific winter storm began producing snow and strong winds in the Sierra Nevada before a multiday blizzard developed.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: WPC's event analysis and contemporaneous AP dispatch corroborate Leap Day onset; later NASA snowpack imagery covers the multiday episode rather than a single day.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Most four-to-eight-foot storm-total snowfall accumulated into March 1–3, not during February 29 alone. Severe blizzard conditions peaked later. Do not claim late-storm totals as Leap Day observations.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original hourly Sierra snowfall and wind-gust timeline with the Leap Day onset highlighted.

alternate_reviews.title: Windstorm Emma approaches Europe on Leap Day
alternate_reviews.location: North Sea coastal region and continental northwest Europe
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On February 29, 2008, Windstorm Emma's system approached northwestern Europe, with a warm front reaching Germany by evening before widespread overnight wind damage.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: KNMI supplies Dutch surface-station and cyclone chronology, while the European Windstorm Catalogue supplies separate ERA-Interim reanalysis-based February 29 pressure and vorticity milestones.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Most destructive Central European gusts and deaths occurred March 1, not February 29. The reanalysis 959.5-hPa low is not an independently measured Dutch station value.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original February 29 UTC pressure/wind chart showing Emma's track and frontal approach.

alternate_reviews.title: A satellite reveals the aftermath of Colorado's historic March blizzard
alternate_reviews.location: Colorado Front Range and adjoining Rocky Mountain states, United States
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On March 20, 2003, NASA Terra MODIS imaged the expansive snow cover left across Colorado and Wyoming by a historic March 18–19 upslope blizzard.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NASA directly observed the snow-cover field on March 20 and CSU independently reviews the previous storm's meteorology; both use common NOAA cooperative/snow reports for totals.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: The March 20 anniversary is satellite acquisition and aftermath, NOT when Denver's main accumulation fell. Do not date 30-inch storm totals to March 20.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original Terra MODIS March 20 snow footprint with surveyed storm totals from March 18–19 separately labeled.

alternate_reviews.title: Satellite imagery reveals the deadly Attica wildfires' footprint
alternate_reviews.location: Attica region near Kineta and Mati, Greece
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On July 24, 2018, satellites documented the destructive Attica wildfire outbreak near Athens after rapid fire growth under hot, dry, windy conditions.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NASA July 24 satellite imagery and EU JRC event-mapping independently describe fire footprint, but may share satellite retrievals.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Kineta and Mati fires ignited July 23. The July 24 anniversary is satellite observation/ongoing response, not ignition. Published satellite products and imagery need rights review.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original July 24 burned-area/satellite active-fire overlay with wind direction and July 23 ignition marked.

alternate_reviews.title: Extreme rain triggers a catastrophic Freetown landslide and flooding
alternate_reviews.location: Regent, Sugar Loaf Mountain, Freetown, Sierra Leone
alternate_reviews.primary_publisher: World Bank Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: Heavy rain during August 14, 2017 contributed to a massive Regent-area slope failure near Freetown, flooding valleys and causing a major humanitarian disaster.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: World Bank-linked assessment records date/impacts, and British Geological Survey separately dates rainfall and studies geomorphology. Human impact estimates changed through later assessments.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: The triggering process involved preceding heavy rain, slope vulnerability and land use; accumulated rainfall is often multiweek. Do not attribute the disaster solely to one day's rainfall or quote conflicting fatality totals.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original Freetown elevation and valley-flow map using site-specific rain timestamps and slope-failure area.

alternate_reviews.title: Typhoon Bopha strikes Mindanao in the southern Philippines
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: Typhoon Bopha (Pablo) made landfall over eastern Mindanao early December 4, 2012 local time, with destructive winds, heavy rain and damaging debris flows.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NASA imagery and JTWC track synthesis corroborate landfall timing; ADRC reports regional impact, while a separate peer-reviewed flood/debris-flow study supports the event geography.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: NASA's 1:12 a.m. Dec 4 Philippine-time satellite scan is 17:12 UTC Dec 3. Do not use UTC-only dates to dispute local landfall date; extreme rainfall maps are multiday and impact totals evolved.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original local/UTC-time Bopha track over Mindanao with storm rainfall and geomorphology caveats.

alternate_reviews.title: Hurricane Matthew passes near Andros Island in the Bahamas
alternate_reviews.secondary_publisher: Bahamas Government statement citing Bahamas Department of Meteorology
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On the morning of October 6, 2016, Hurricane Matthew's center passed near Andros and New Providence in the Bahamas, bringing hurricane conditions.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: Contemporaneous NHC advisory and Bahamian Prime Minister statement citing local meteorological reports corroborate passage. Both share some best-track satellite information.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: October 5–6 island passage has local and UTC date shifts; distinguish observed center tracks, forecast surge and later impact estimates, and do not transfer Grand Bahama impacts to Andros.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original 2016 GOES and NHC track reconstruction across Andros/New Providence.

editorial_deferrals.reason: The February 2012 Upper Midwest blizzard may share the same synoptic system as the main February 2012 tornado outbreak; chosen instead were separate-year 2024 Sierra blizzard and 2008 European Emma.
2018 Attica fires ignited July 23; selected 24 July satellite acquisition/ongoing burning rather than misleading ignition claim.
Denver main snow fell March18–19; selected March20 original satellite snow cover milestone.
